hero.title: 15 questions to understand why you can't find love
hero.description: You have been single for a while and you don't understand why. This test looks at the people you meet, what you expect and what holds you back, and puts a name on what gets in the way. Free, instant result.
hero.subtitle: Fifteen questions, two minutes, nobody sees your answers

section1.title: Why you can't find love: what this test looks at
section1.intro: You have been single for a while. You are not fussy, you are not asking for the moon, and yet it doesn't happen.
section1.p1: The question "why can't I find love?" comes up for a lot of people, and often at the same moment: after a relationship that didn't work out, or when all your friends are pairing up. So you start looking for an explanation. Too demanding? Not good enough? Just unlucky? Most of the time, it is none of the three.
section1.p2: This test asks fifteen questions about situations you know: a party where you don't know anyone, someone you like who doesn't tick your boxes, a message that goes unanswered, a relationship that gets serious. Your answers draw a picture of what happens between you and meeting someone.
section1.p3: At the end, you get a result on four levels, from the simplest (you lack opportunities) to the deepest (the place is still taken). Each level comes with a reading and a lead. It doesn't say who you are, it says what gets in the way today. And that can change! And if your question is rather where your single life comes from day to day, between missing chances, social life and the fear of approaching, another test takes care of that.

section2.title: The six reasons that come up most
section2.pillar1Text: This is the most ordinary reason, and the most common. Between work, home and the same friends, you can go months without talking to someone new. No app replaces that.
section2.pillar2Title: A list that is too precise
section2.pillar2Text: Age, height, job, city, the way they dress... Each criterion can be defended, but put together they let nobody through. And they often describe someone you have already known.
section2.pillar3Title: An ex who is still there
section2.pillar3Text: You can be single for two years and not be free. As long as you compare, as long as you watch what the other person is up to, the place is taken. New people feel it, even without knowing it.
section2.pillar4Title: The fear that it gets serious
section2.pillar4Text: Everything goes well for three weeks, then you find flaws, you slow down, you drift away. It isn't boredom, it's protection. It often comes from an old story, in a relationship or in the family.
section2.pillar5Text: When a good person shows interest in you and your first thought is "they'll be disappointed", you are already losing. You make yourself less available, you test the other person, you withdraw before being left.
section2.pillar6Title: A way of attaching that scares people off, or runs away
section2.pillar6Text: Some people attach too fast and too hard, needing reassurance with every message. Others pull away as soon as the other person gets close. Both ways of attaching are learned early, and both can be understood.

section3.title: What we tell ourselves, and what is going on
section3.intro: The same single life can be told several ways. Here is what people often tell themselves, and what it usually hides.
section3.row1Level: A week without a new face
section3.row1Analysis: A regular activity, not one more party
section3.row2Level: A list that describes an ex
section3.row2Analysis: A date outside your criteria, just to see
section3.row3Level: Distance as soon as it gets serious
section3.row3Analysis: Stay one more week, and watch what happens
section3.row4Analysis: Let the other person decide whether they are disappointed
section3.row5Analysis: Ask yourself what you are protecting yourself from

section4.title: Where to start, depending on your result
section4.p1: The result puts you on a level. Here is the first thing to do for each one.
section4.sub1P1: Change the scenery once a week: a class, a club, a team sport, a place where you run into the same people several times. Repetition is what creates encounters, not the one-off big night out.
section4.sub2Title: A reflex is slowing you down
section4.sub2P1: Do the opposite of what you usually do, just once. Get in touch first. Say yes to someone who didn't make an impression right away. Most solid couples did not start with love at first sight.
section4.sub3P1: Look for where the protection comes from before forcing it. A test on the way you attach is a good starting point, and if the word "future" makes you step back, fear of commitment is easier to understand than people think.
section4.sub4P1: Don't force the encounter. Deal first with what is taking up the space: an ex, a lack, a fear. And talk about it, to a friend or a professional. It isn't an admission of weakness, it's just faster with two.
section4.tip: This test is about you, not about other people. If what you are really wondering is what one specific person feels, finding out whether they secretly love you is another question, and another test.

section5.title: How this test works
section5.p1: Fifteen situations, four answers each time, from the most open to the most closed. There is no right answer: reply the way you actually do things, not the way you wish you did. It takes two minutes.
section5.p2: Each answer counts for points, and some questions weigh more: the ones about your ex, about what happens when things get serious and about what you think you are worth. Those are the ones that say the most. Your score puts you on one of four levels, each with a reading and a lead.

seo.faq1Q: Why can't I find love when I'm doing everything I can?
seo.faq1A: Because "everything" is often the same thing repeated: the same apps, the same nights out, the same type of person. This test looks precisely at what repeats. And sometimes, making a lot of effort is a way of not looking at what blocks underneath: the fear that it might work, or a story that isn't finished.
seo.faq2Q: Is it normal to be single at 30, or at 40?
seo.faq2A: Yes. The age at which people settle down has been rising for years, and many people go through several single periods in their life. What matters is not the age, it is whether being single suits you or weighs on you. If it is other people's opinion that weighs, the problem is not yours.
seo.faq3Q: Why don't men, or women, like me?
seo.faq3A: Most of the time, it isn't about being likeable. Someone who doubts themselves makes themselves less available, listens less, tests the other person without realising it, and the other person feels it. The test has several questions about this. If the result points to self-esteem, that is where to start, not with your appearance.
seo.faq4A: Many women ask themselves this, often after a remark heard once. A confident person with a full life scares off those who were looking for someone to dominate. That is not a loss. What can get in the way, on the other hand, is running a first date like a job interview. That is question ten of the test.
seo.faq5Q: Am I made for a relationship or for being on my own?
seo.faq5A: Some people are happy on their own, and this test does not try to convince them otherwise. The difference shows in one thing: does being single suit you, or does it protect you? If you are fine on your own and meeting someone doesn't scare you, you are made for what you are living. If you are fine on your own "at least", that little phrase is worth a look.
seo.faq6Q: How do I meet someone when I don't go out?
seo.faq6A: By making regular what isn't. A weekly activity where you see the same people again does more than ten nights out. Apps can help, as long as you move quickly to a real date. And for that first date, having a few questions to ask keeps it from turning into a job interview.
